# Recorded API fixtures

Response shapes recorded from real servers (plex-safety rule 11). Identifying values
(names, ids, tokens, hostnames) are sanitized; structure and field names are verbatim.

> **XML fixtures must NOT use a bare `.xml` extension — use `.xml.txt`.** Unraid Community
> Applications scans every `*.xml` file in the repo looking for app templates, and flags any that
> isn't one as `not_unraid_application`, which shows as a failed check on our CA submission. The
> content is still plain XML; only the filename differs.

| File                              | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Recorded   |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------- |
| `pms_managed_hubs.xml.txt`        | PMS 1.43.3.10896 `GET /hubs/sections/1/manage` (XML), the endpoint `LibrarySection.managedHubs()` reads — captured off SFLIX's Movies library, 70 hubs reduced to 8, titles neutralised (the real ones name individual people, via each row's per-account title marker). Settles what `is_collection_hub` matches: a COLLECTION's hub is `custom.collection.<sectionID>.<ratingKey>` here (a single ratingKey — the DOUBLED form in `pms_hubs_shared_account.json` is `/hubs`, a different endpoint), and built-in hubs use their own families (`movie.recentlyadded`, `recent.library.playlists`). Built-ins DO carry all three `promotedTo*` flags, so the guard's fail-open path is belt-and-braces rather than load-bearing; `deletable` is present on collections and absent on built-ins. **Note what is NOT here: not one collection on this server had `promotedToRecommended=0`.** Every hub with all three flags off is a built-in the owner switched off. So either Plex promotes a new collection to Recommended by default, or an off-shelf collection is absent from this listing entirely — unresolved, and it bears on whether issue #106's anchor case is reachable in practice | 2026-08-30 |
| `pms_managed_hub_renamed_collection.json` | PMS 1.43.4.10903 — one Shortlist row's collection read three ways moments after an in-place rename, off SFLIX's Movies library: `GET /hubs/sections/1/manage`, `GET /library/metadata/<ratingKey>` and `GET /hubs/sections/1`. ratingKey neutralised, per-account title markers stripped. Settles why `place_rows` identifies a hub by the ratingKey in its identifier and not by title: **the manage listing keeps the title the collection had when it was promoted**, while the collection and the hub viewers are served both carry the new one. Matched by title, a renamed row reads as somebody else's collection. On SFLIX 15 of 93 promoted rows in one library were in that state after one night | 2026-09-16 |

| `plextv_resources.json`           | plex.tv `GET /api/v2/resources?includeHttps=1` — the shape behind `auth.owned_machine_ids()`, which decides who may sign in to an unclaimed instance and which server they may link. Captured owned entry is real; the `owned:false` and player entries are synthesised (this account has no inbound shares) and labelled as such in `_why`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | 2026-07-29 |
| `pms_watched_incremental.xml.txt` | PMS 1.43.3 `GET /library/sections/{key}/all` — the watched read, plus a measured table of which query params this server honours. The headline: `unwatched=0` and `sort=lastViewedAt:desc` work, while **every cutoff-filter form (`lastViewedAt>=`, `>>=`, and a `year>>=` control) is silently ignored** and returns the full set with a 200. That is why the incremental watch-history read narrows by ordering + an early stop rather than by a filter                                                                                                                                 | 2026-07-30 |
| `plextv_combined_filters.json`    | plex.tv `PUT /api/users/{id}` + `GET /api/users` — proof that share-filter strings are stored and returned VERBATIM: `\|`/`&` between conditions and `,`/`%2C` between values all round-trip byte-identical, with no normalization. So the shape Shortlist reads is whichever writer last touched that account (Plex Web, plexapi, or us), which is the whole of issue #77. Written to a canary account with its original value snapshotted and restored                                                                                                                                   | 2026-08-10 |
| `pms_collections_listing.json`    | PMS 1.43.3 `GET /library/sections/{key}/all?type=18` vs `GET /library/collections/{rk}` — the collections LISTING carries **no** `<Label>` children (103 collections, zero labels); they exist only on the per-collection detail read, which plexapi fetches silently behind `collection.labels`. Every label-based read in Shortlist depends on that, and a successful-but-empty read is indistinguishable from an unlabelled row — which is why the sweep both re-reads per collection and refuses to act when NO row reads as labelled, and why the fake now serves the same two shapes | 2026-08-10 |
| `pms_collection_field_edits.json` | PMS 1.43.4 `PUT /library/sections/{key}/all?type=18&id=…&summary.value=…&titleSort.value=…` (plexapi `Collection.edit`) on a throwaway collection in SFLIX's TV library, created and deleted by the probe. Settles how issue #120 must write a row's summary and sort title: a LOCKED sort title survives a title edit and a membership write (so Shortlist re-applies it after a rename), an UNLOCKED custom one is overwritten by the next title edit (so it is locked), a blank unlocked one is rebuilt by Plex from the full title with its leading emoji kept, the summary round-trips byte-exact, labels are untouched, and a field edit costs ~0.01–0.09s where a label write there took 21.9s | 2026-09-13 |
| `pms_hubs_shared_account.json`    | PMS 1.43.3 `GET /hubs` fetched with a SHARED account's own server token, on a server carrying 46 per-person rows. Settles two things that were assumed. A promoted row appears as its OWN hub — identity lives in `key` (`/library/collections/<id>/children`), and there are **no** `Metadata` entries of type `collection` to look for. And a real PMS **does** apply a share `label!=` filter to `/hubs`: this account's Home carried its own four rows, the shared row, and other tools' collections, and not one of the other 45 people's rows. That is the filter-enforcement canary's whole premise, previously untested. Reduced from 33 hubs to 11 and from 6 Metadata items per hub to 2 (with `size`/`hubKey` reduced to match); titles neutralised, including two "Because you watched X" rows that named a real person's viewing — see the file's `_sanitized` | 2026-08-18 |
| `overseerr_media_page.json`       | Seerr 3.4.1 (`seerr-team/seerr`) `GET /api/v1/media`, recorded 2026-09-02 off a live 26,941-row instance — one row per (mediaType, status) actually present, plus the single row that was genuinely downloading. Settles three things the specs get wrong. **`mediaType` is real** (present on all 5,000 sampled rows, absent from the published `MediaInfo` schema) and load-bearing, since TMDB's movie and tv id spaces overlap. **The status enum is not what any spec says**: the server's own code has `BLOCKLISTED=6, DELETED=7`, while Overseerr's spec AND Seerr's own shipped `seerr-api.yml` both say `6=DELETED` and document nothing above 6 — yet 821 of 5,000 rows were status 7. And **PROCESSING does not mean downloading**: 76 rows were PROCESSING and exactly ONE was moving, which is why `downloadStatus` decides that word. Sanitized: serviceUrl hosts, Plex machine ids, downloadStatus titles, long season arrays trimmed | 2026-09-02 |
| `overseerr_users_page.json`       | Seerr 3.4.1 `GET /api/v1/user` — key set, null pattern and pageInfo recorded 2026-09-02 from a 62-account instance; the identities are FABRICATED (the real ones are 62 real people). What it settles: **`username` was null on all 62**, so every account names itself with `displayName` + `plexUsername` — and `displayName` is the field the published `User` schema omits. That is why the client falls through `displayName` → `username` → `plexUsername` → `email` rather than trusting the documented field | 2026-09-02 |
| `tmdb_discover_paged.json`        | TMDB API v3 `GET /discover/movie` (pages 1 and 34 of 34) and `GET /discover/tv`, with the Halloween season's keywords OR'd by `\|`, recorded 2026-09-15 for seasonal rows (discussion #124); 2 results per page, overviews cut. Settles how a season's title list is read. Pages carry `total_pages`/`total_results`. **Paging by `popularity.desc` silently loses titles** (Christmas: 3,133 unique ids over 3,370 results, because popularity moves between page reads) while `primary_release_date.asc` (`first_air_date.asc` for TV) returns all 3,370. **A page above 500 answers HTTP 400**, so a list is read to `min(total_pages, 500)` | 2026-09-15 |
| `overseerr_requests_page.json`    | Seerr 3.4.1 `GET /api/v1/request?filter=all&sort=added`, recorded 2026-09-28 off a live instance (7 requests, 6 people); identities FABRICATED with ids remapped consistently across the three `*_request_tags.json` / `overseerr_*` files of the same date. Settles what a "Your requests" row (issue #127) reads: **`requestedBy.plexId` is on every request** and equals `users.plex_account_id`, so a request maps to a person with no name matching; `status` 5 (COMPLETED) is set by Seerr itself when the media lands, and for a TV request only when every requested season is available, each `seasons[].status` flipping first; `media.mediaAddedAt` is when Plex first saw the title; `media` carries no title | 2026-09-28 |
| `overseerr_arr_settings.json`     | Seerr 3.4.1 `GET /api/v1/settings/radarr` + `/sonarr`, recorded 2026-09-28. Settles that **`tagRequests` is a readable key** (absent from the published schema) — the switch that makes Seerr stamp `<seerrUserId>-<username>` on each Radarr/Sonarr item it sends, which is what lets a deleted request still be traced to a person | 2026-09-28 |
| `radarr_request_tags.json`        | Radarr v3 `GET /api/v3/tag` + `GET /api/v3/movie`, recorded 2026-09-28 (10,168 movies, 48 tags, 5 Seerr requester tags on 7 movies; items cut to the keys a requests row reads, titles neutralised). Settles the requester tag FORMAT (`<seerr user id>-<username>`, matched on the number only) and that **a tag survives the Seerr request being deleted**: 3 of the 7 tagged films had no request left in Seerr and every one still carried its tag | 2026-09-28 |
| `sonarr_request_tags.json`        | Sonarr v3 `GET /api/v3/tag` + `GET /api/v3/series`, same recording as above (4,966 series, 63 tags, 3 requester tags on 4 series). Same format and same survival: 3 of 4 tagged shows had their request deleted | 2026-09-28 |
| `pms_collection_children.xml.txt` | PMS 1.43.4.10903 `GET /library/collections/{rk}/children?includeGuids=1` (what plexapi's `Collection.items()` issues), off a regular 50-film collection in SFLIX's Movies library, cut to 4 films; file paths neutralised. Settles what a custom season (issue #137) reads from an owner's collection: **every member carries its `tmdb://` guid inline**, so one read maps a collection to TMDB ids with no per-film re-read (every member of 46 to 1,187-film collections, smart and regular, on the same server). The container carries only `size`, no `totalSize` | 2026-10-02 |
| `pms_section_title_search.xml.txt` | PMS 1.43.4.10903 `GET /library/sections/{key}/all?includeGuids=1&title=free` with `X-Plex-Container-Size: 5` (plexapi's `LibrarySection.search(title=…, maxresults=5)`), off SFLIX's Movies library; file paths neutralised, and one Shortlist row's title (a person's watch plus their account marker) replaced. Settles the season editor's film search: **`title=` is a substring match** (5 of `totalSize` 21), every result carries its `tmdb://` guid, and a result lists Shortlist's own rows among its `<Collection>` tags | 2026-10-02 |
